finding.claim: UpyunCallbackAuth does not abort after a failed signature validation. It writes a 401 at line 86, then calls c.Next() at line 89 unconditionally, so the upload-completion handler still runs for an unsigned callback.
finding.source: Unsigned POST body to /api/v4/callback/upyun/:sessionID/:key (router.go:491-496). The attacker needs a valid sessionID and key for a pending Upyun upload session; the callback URL is part of the upload policy, so the session's uploader has it.
finding.sink: ProcessCallback (callback.go:17-31) calls callback.ProcessCallback(c), which finalizes the upload session. That function is in service/callback and is not in this repo.

trace.note: middleware.UseUploadSession(PolicyTypeUpyun) loads the session. Code not in repo, unverified.
Session is read from the gin context.
upyun.ValidateCallback is called; on signature failure it returns an error.
c.JSON(401, ...) is written, with no return and no c.Abort().
c.Next() runs the remaining handler chain regardless of the failure.
ProcessCallback(http.StatusBadRequest, false) runs and completes the upload from the request body.

finding.guards_checked: UseUploadSession (not in repo, unverified). Signature check upyun.ValidateCallback fails but its result is ignored. Contrast: OSSCallbackValidate (callback.go:64-68,73-76) and QiniuCallbackValidate (callback.go:42-51) both Abort and return on failure.
